title: Day 64 · Week 9, Day 1 — Brain: the plate — the first layer of the thinking brain appears this week, the ropes the neurons climb, the inside-out rule, the waiting room that is bigger in humans than in anything else, the ear that closes its coil, and the virus in toddler saliva that only a father's hands can keep out
summary: Week 9, Day 1 is post-fertilization day 50, the turn from Carnegie stage 20 to 21 (20–24 mm). The Day 57 neuron factory now has a destination: the cortical plate, the embryonic cortex, which Meyer's 2000 human series shows emerging at stage 21, within a day or two of today. Neurons born at the ventricular surface climb radial glial fibres (Rakic 1972, 1988) and settle inside-out, deepest layers first (Angevine & Sidman 1961). Beneath the plate a transient subplate forms, the thalamic axons' waiting room, larger in humans than in any other species (Kostović & Judaš 2010; Molnár 2019). The cochlea completes its coil this week, hair cells differentiate at 10–12 weeks, function begins at 18–20 weeks, and the first behavioural responses to sound appear at 19 weeks (Pujol 1991; Hepper & Shahidullah 1994). Three things with human evidence reach the climbing neurons: alcohol, whose mechanism is disrupted proliferation and migration (Miller 1986) and whose US burden is 1.1–5.0% of first-graders (May 2018); valproate, 11 IQ points at age 6 (Meador 2013) and 9.8% malformations (Cochrane 2023); and cytomegalovirus, which infects 1 in 200 newborns and leaves 1 in 5 of them with permanent problems, mostly hearing (CDC), is caught from the saliva and urine of young children, and against which a hygiene briefing cut new maternal infections from 7.6% to 1.2% (Revello 2015). The father's lever: take the toddler's diapers, plates and pacifiers until Day 280.
action: Ten minutes tonight, in two parts. One: answer the toddler question out loud with your partner — is there a child under five she will be handling regularly between now and Day 280 (yours, a niece or nephew, a classroom, a nursery, a ward)? If no, write 'CMV: low exposure' on the Us page of the Day 61 file and move on. If yes, write Revello's list under it: soap after diapers and noses; no shared cups, cutlery, food, toothbrushes or pacifiers; no kisses on the mouth; no co-sleeping with the toddler — and in your handwriting, 'diapers, potty, plates, pacifiers: his.' Two: add question sixteen to the Day 40 list: 'Given her exposure to young children, should she have a CMV antibody test, and what would you do with either answer?' Bring it to the next visit.
